title: A Thin Thread of Light
paragraphs: Before electric lights, people used candles and oil lamps at night. These gave weak light, made smoke, and could easily start fires. In the nineteenth century, many inventors tried to make light with electricity. It was a hard problem.

A light bulb works in a simple way. Electricity passes through a very thin thread inside the glass. The thread gets so hot that it starts to glow. The air is taken out of the bulb, because air would make the hot thread burn up quickly. The hardest part was finding a thread that could glow for a long time.

In 1879, Thomas Edison and his team in the United States made a bulb that lasted for many hours. They tested many materials before they found good ones. At about the same time, Joseph Swan in England made a similar bulb. So the light bulb was not the work of just one person. Today, many homes use LED bulbs, which need much less energy.
